summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with acute left neck pain that began after cracking his neck, later associated with fevers and neurological symptoms. Initial imaging ruled out dissection, but blood cultures revealed Streptococcus bovis bacteremia. MRI showed findings concerning for osteomyelitis and septic arthritis of the left claviculomanubrial joint. Due to a penicillin allergy, he underwent successful ceftriaxone desensitization in the MICU and was started on a six-week course of IV antibiotics via PICC line. A colonoscopy identified and removed five colonic adenomas, likely the source of bacteremia. Warfarin was discontinued as his prior pulmonary embolism was provoked and adequately treated. His pain resolved with multimodal management, and he was discharged home with nursing support, stable vital signs, and clear mental status.
problems: Septic arthritis of the sternoclavicular joint
